Cc: secops@acmehealth.com

Subject: Request: hosting perimeter confirmation + private peering readiness for EU pilot

Hi David,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. As part of our SIG/CAIQ review and internal procurement checklist, we need a concise confirmation of Redwood's hosting perimeter for the EU pilot we talked about (EU-1 region) and a short runbook for establishing private peering (VPC peering / Private Service Connect) to our VNets. Specifically we need:

- Confirmation that customer workloads can be pinned to EU-1 (no transitive egress to non-EU regions)
- High-level network diagram for private peering + expected BGP/IP ranges
- KMS partitioning details (are keys region-scoped?)
- Expected timeline for provisioning a private peering session (and any approvals)
- Any SOC 2 / SIG evidence snippets relevant to network segregation (we do not need full reports, just infra excerpts)

We'd like to kick a short pilot next month; could you share a single PDF "perimeter + peering runbook" and a CIDR worksheet we can pass to our network team? Attaching our intake form in a follow-up.

Best,
Asha Rao
Security Architect, Acme Health
[Attachment: acme_intake_form.xlsx]

From: david_kim@redwood.ai
To: acme-security@acmehealth.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: hosting perimeter confirmation + private peering readiness for EU pilot

Asha — thanks, and appreciate the clear checklist.

We can absolutely support the EU-1 pinning plus a parallel APAC staging lane for performance testing. Attached is a short runbook and a CIDR worksheet for handoff. High-level answers inline below and the engineering team (cc'd) will follow up with the technical specifics and timeline: 

- Pinning: Yes — for Private deployment and Dedicated pools you can pin compute to EU-1. For Hosted API we provide region routing policy but the public multi-tenant layer may include cross-region control-plane traffic for telemetry; we will call that out in the runbook.
- Private peering: We support both VPC peering (cloud-native) and Private Service Connect-style endpoints. The runbook lists the required BGP setup and pre-approved CIDR ranges.
- KMS: Customer KMS integration is region-scoped. If you bring your key (BYOK) we recommend provisioning it in EU-1.
- Timeline: Typical turn-up for private peering is 5–10 business days once joint firewall rules and CIDR worksheet are agreed.
- SOC 2 / SIG: See attached soc2-infra-excerpt.pdf for network segregation evidence; we can provide a redacted SIG/CAIQ snapshot in the next business day.

Next step: Priyom — can you confirm the expected BGP community behavior and whether we need a formal change window for EU-1 peering (customer wants a pilot on 04/05)?

David Kim
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_private_peering_runbook.pdf]

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: david_kim@redwood.ai, acme-security@acmehealth.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 08:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: hosting perimeter confirmation + private peering readiness for EU pilot

Hi all — technical details below and I've attached a staging CIDR workbook tailored to Acme's intake. TL;DR: no mandatory maintenance window for initial session; BGP session established over IPSec, full list below.

Attachment: eu1-apac-staging-cidr-plan.xlsx (sheets: acme-intake, redwood-cidrs, bgp-template)

Key points:
- CIDR ranges: Redwood reserves 10.10.0.0/16 (EU-1) and 10.11.0.0/16 (APAC-staging) for private endpoints. We ask customers to provide a /20 range to avoid overlaps.
- BGP: We accept EBGP sessions over IPSec; advertise only customer-advertised prefixes. Community tagging optional (we support 65012:xxxx for routing policies).
- KMS: BYOK supported via regional HSM; key metadata and access logs are stored in-region in EU-1. Audit logs are available via the console and exported to a customer-controlled S3/GCS bucket on request.
- Telemetry & control-plane: Control-plane calls (for scheduling/metrics) transit our control plane but payloads are pinned; runbook sections 3.1–3.4 explain encryption-in-transit and at-rest boundaries.
- Fallbacks: We provide an automatic model-variant fallback to a compatible hosted variant in another region only if the customer approves a cross-region fallback policy. By default that is disabled for EU-pinned workloads.

Provisioning timeline (conservative):
- Day 0–1: Intake & CIDR confirmation
- Day 2–4: Network changes & mutual firewall rule validation
- Day 5–10: BGP session + integration smoke tests

I'll own the pilot turn-up and will schedule a 30-minute netops call next week.

--
Priyom Das
Lead SRE, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: bgp-template.txt]
